title: Counting carbohydrates (bread units)
what: This is a way to count how many carbohydrates are in food. Carbohydrates affect blood sugar the most.
why: With diabetes, especially if you take insulin before meals.
duration: learning usually takes a few days of practice
tell_doctor: How many units of insulin you need per bread unit, which your doctor decides
If your sugar after meals is often high or low
If you want to change your diet

prepare.title: Chart
prepare.text: Get a bread unit chart from your doctor or a diabetes school.

prepare.title: Scale
prepare.text: A kitchen scale helps at first.

prepare.title: Labels
prepare.text: On the package, look at the line for carbohydrates per 100 grams.

steps: One bread unit is usually 10 to 12 grams of carbohydrates, so check how your doctor counts
Find the food in the chart or on the package
Weigh the portion or estimate it using the chart
Count the bread units on the whole plate
Add up all the foods in that meal
Choose your insulin dose only by the plan your doctor gave you
Check your sugar 2 hours after the meal and write it down
feel: At first it seems hard, then you count by eye
Sometimes you make mistakes, which is normal, and the diary will help
after: Show your diary to your doctor
Meat, fish, and eggs have almost no carbohydrates
Sweet drinks and juices give a lot of carbohydrates quickly

faq.q: Do I need to count if I take pills?
faq.a: It is still useful, so that your meals stay steady. Ask your doctor how exactly you need to count.
Most vegetables are barely counted. Potatoes, corn, and beans must be counted.

reminders.text: Before you eat, count the bread units and write them in your diary.
